title: When Angi Actually Works (The One Case We'll Defend)
meta: Angi isn't always a trap. The one scenario where buying shared leads makes sense — new shop, no pipeline, instant phone response (MIT Sloan 2026 on speed-to-lead).
short: There's exactly one situation where Angi earns its keep: you're brand new, you have no pipeline yet, and you answer every lead in minutes. Outside that, your money builds more when you own the lead.
statLabel: More likely to connect when you respond in 5 minutes vs 30 (MIT Sloan 2026)

body.answer: New, hungry, and fast on the phone — that's the window.
body.html: If you just hung your shingle, have no reviews, no referral base, and no website traffic, a shared-lead platform can put at-bats in front of you today. That's real value when the alternative is silence. The catch: it only works if you treat speed like oxygen.

body.answer: First to respond usually wins the job.
body.html: On shared leads, the homeowner is calling several pros. Responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect (MIT Sloan 2026), and most people hire whoever they reach first. If you're on a roof and can't answer, you're funding your competitor's close.

body.h2: Treat it as a bridge, not a home
body.answer: Use the cash flow to build assets you own.
body.html: Every dollar Angi makes you should buy you independence: reviews, a referral system, a website that turns visitors into calls. Those are exclusive leads that don't disappear when you stop paying. Angi is the ladder, not the house.

body.answer: This one came straight off the podcast.
body.html: Marshall and Ray went deep on this in Is Angi Worth It? on Get Booked, Not F***ed — same math, more cussing. Watch or listen to the full episode here.

faq.q: Is Angi ever a good idea?
faq.a: Yes — for a brand-new shop with no pipeline that can answer every lead in minutes. Speed drives everything: 5 minutes vs 30 is up to 100x on connection rate (MIT Sloan 2026).

faq.q: How fast do I have to respond to Angi leads?
faq.a: Minutes, not hours. The homeowner is calling several pros, and most hire whoever they reach first.

faq.q: When should I stop using Angi?
faq.a: Once your reviews, referrals, and website are generating exclusive leads. At that point shared leads are the more expensive option per booked job.
